title: Commercial property and business income
summary: How a commercial property coverage part is built, Basic vs Broad vs Special, vacancy, coinsurance math, business income and key endorsements.
objectives: Tell what the Broad and Special causes of loss forms add to Basic
Apply the vacancy rule and work a coinsurance problem
Separate Business Income from Extra Expense and their start times
Match condo, builders risk, legal liability and the selected endorsements

scenes.title: Commercial property and business income
scenes.subtitle: Coverage forms, causes of loss, coinsurance and time element coverage

beats.text: Commercial property questions love numbers: 60 days, 15%, 72 hours, 80%. Let's see where each one comes from.
beats.say: Commercial property questions love numbers: sixty days, fifteen percent, seventy-two hours, eighty percent. Let's see where each one comes from.

scenes.title: How a commercial property part is built
scenes.src: ISO CP 00 90 07 88, D.; MCL 500.2833(1)(q); ISO CP 00 10 10 12, A.1; vs-vs_commercial-05

items.label: Commercial Property Conditions
items.detail: Shared conditions; suit within 2 years after the loss (Michigan tolls it)

items.label: Coverage form
items.detail: Building and Personal Property: building, your property, others' property

items.label: Causes of loss form
items.detail: You choose Basic, Broad or Special

beats.text: Commercial property keeps shared conditions in a separate form. The 1988 version allows 2 years after the loss to sue; Michigan pauses that clock from notice until denial.
beats.say: Commercial property keeps shared conditions in a separate form. The nineteen eighty-eight version allows two years after the loss to sue; Michigan pauses that clock from notice until denial.

beats.text: The main coverage form is Building and Personal Property. It covers the building, your business personal property in it or within 100 feet, and others' property in your care.
beats.say: The main coverage form is Building and Personal Property. It covers the building, your business personal property in it or within one hundred feet, and others' property in your care.

beats.text: Then you choose a causes of loss form: Basic, Broad or Special.
beats.say: Then you choose a causes of loss form: Basic, Broad or Special.

scenes.title: Causes of loss: Basic, Broad, Special

columns.name: Basic
points: Fire, lightning, explosion, windstorm or hail
Smoke, aircraft or vehicles, riot or civil commotion, vandalism
Sprinkler leakage, sinkhole collapse, volcanic action

columns.name: Broad
points: Plus weight of snow, ice or sleet
Plus water damage, and collapse coverage

columns.name: Special
points: Direct physical loss unless excluded or limited
The only one that covers theft
Theft limits: $2,500 furs or jewelry; $250 stamps or tickets

scenes.tell: Basic is 11 named perils. Broad adds falling objects, weight of snow, ice or sleet, and water damage. Special is open perils.

beats.text: The 2012 Basic form names 11 perils: fire, lightning, explosion, windstorm or hail, smoke, aircraft or vehicles, riot or civil commotion, vandalism, sprinkler leakage, sinkhole collapse and volcanic action.
beats.say: The twenty twelve Basic form names eleven perils: fire, lightning, explosion, windstorm or hail, smoke, aircraft or vehicles, riot or civil commotion, vandalism, sprinkler leakage, sinkhole collapse and volcanic action.

beats.text: Broad is Basic plus a Michigan winter: falling objects, weight of snow, ice or sleet, and water damage from a system or appliance. It also adds collapse coverage.
beats.say: Broad is Basic plus a Michigan winter: falling objects, weight of snow, ice or sleet, and water damage from a system or appliance. It also adds collapse coverage.

beats.text: The 2017 Special form covers direct physical loss unless excluded or limited. It's the only one of the three that covers theft, with special theft limits.
beats.say: The twenty seventeen Special form covers direct physical loss unless excluded or limited. It's the only one of the three that covers theft, with special theft limits.

beats.text: Watch out: sprinkler leakage and sinkhole collapse are already Basic perils.
beats.say: Watch out: sprinkler leakage and sinkhole collapse are already Basic perils.

scenes.q: On a calm day, a tree limb falls through a store's roof. Which is the narrowest causes of loss form that covers the damage?
scenes.why: Falling objects is one of the perils Broad adds to Basic. Special covers it too, but Broad is the narrowest form that does.

beats.text: Quick check. On a calm day, a tree limb falls through a store's roof. Which is the narrowest causes of loss form that covers it? Pick an answer.
beats.say: Quick check. On a calm day, a tree limb falls through a store's roof. Which is the narrowest causes of loss form that covers it? Pick an answer.

reveal.text: Broad. Falling objects is a peril Broad adds. Special covers it too, but Broad is narrower.
reveal.say: Broad. Falling objects is a peril Broad adds. Special covers it too, but Broad is narrower.

scenes.title: Vacancy: more than 60 days
scenes.src: ISO CP 00 10 10 12, E.6 (2012 Building and Personal Property form)

items.label: Not paid at all
items.detail: Vandalism, sprinkler leakage unless protected from freezing, glass breakage, water damage, theft

items.label: Owner's building: the 31% rule
items.detail: Not vacant if at least 31% is rented and used, or used by the owner

beats.text: Vacancy is a loss condition in the 2012 Building and Personal Property form. It applies when the building was vacant more than 60 consecutive days before the loss.
beats.say: Vacancy is a loss condition in the twenty twelve Building and Personal Property form. It applies when the building was vacant more than sixty consecutive days before the loss.

beats.text: Then some losses aren't paid at all: vandalism, sprinkler leakage unless protected against freezing, building glass breakage, water damage, and theft or attempted theft.
beats.say: Then some losses aren't paid at all: vandalism, sprinkler leakage unless protected against freezing, building glass breakage, water damage, and theft or attempted theft.

beats.text: Any other covered loss is paid minus 15%.
beats.say: Any other covered loss is paid minus fifteen percent.

beats.text: For an owner, the building isn't vacant if at least 31% is rented and used by tenants, or used by the owner, for customary operations.
beats.say: For an owner, the building isn't vacant if at least thirty-one percent is rented and used by tenants, or used by the owner, for customary operations.

scenes.title: Coinsurance: Did over Should
scenes.hook: Did over Should, times the Loss; take off the Deductible, and that's the insurer's cost.
items: Should: value at the time of loss times the coinsurance percentage
Did: the limit of insurance you actually carried
Did over Should, times the loss, minus the deductible
Never more than the limit; no penalty if Did is at least Should

beats.text: Now coinsurance. Here's the hook: Did over Should, times the Loss; take off the Deductible, and that's the insurer's cost.
beats.say: Now coinsurance. Here's the hook: Did over Should, times the Loss; take off the Deductible, and that's the insurer's cost.

beats.text: Should is the value at the time of loss times the coinsurance percentage. Did is the limit you carried.
beats.say: Should is the value at the time of loss times the coinsurance percentage. Did is the limit you carried.

beats.text: Divide, multiply by the loss, and subtract the deductible. Never more than the limit, and no penalty if Did meets Should.
beats.say: Divide, multiply by the loss, and subtract the deductible. Never more than the limit, and no penalty if Did meets Should.

scenes.title: Coinsurance worked example
scenes.src: ISO CP 00 10 10 12, F.1 (2012 Building and Personal Property form)
given: Building value at time of loss: $400,000

beats.text: Let's work one. A Kalamazoo warehouse is worth $400,000 at the time of loss, with 80% coinsurance. So it should carry $320,000.
beats.say: Let's work one. A Kalamazoo warehouse is worth four hundred thousand dollars at the time of loss, with eighty percent coinsurance. So it should carry three hundred twenty thousand dollars.

beats.text: It carries only $240,000. Did over Should is 0.75.
beats.say: It carries only two hundred forty thousand dollars. Did over Should is zero point seven five.

beats.text: A loss of $60,000 times 0.75 is $45,000.
beats.say: A loss of sixty thousand dollars times zero point seven five is forty-five thousand dollars.

beats.text: Subtract the deductible of $1,000, and the insurer pays $44,000.
beats.say: Subtract the deductible of one thousand dollars, and the insurer pays forty-four thousand dollars.

scenes.title: Business Income vs Extra Expense
scenes.src: ISO CP 00 30 10 12, A.1-2, A.5.c, D., F.3 (2012 Business Income and Extra Expense form)

columns.name: Business Income
points: Lost net income plus continuing expenses, including payroll
Starts 72 hours after the direct physical loss
Extended Business Income: up to 60 days after reopening

columns.name: Extra Expense
points: Extra costs to avoid or minimize the shutdown
Like moving to a temporary location

scenes.tell: Lost profit and continuing bills while closed: Business Income. Extra money spent to keep going: Extra Expense.

beats.text: Now time element coverage, from the 2012 Business Income form. It pays lost net income plus continuing operating expenses, including payroll.
beats.say: Now time element coverage, from the twenty twelve Business Income form. It pays lost net income plus continuing operating expenses, including payroll.

beats.text: Its period of restoration starts 72 hours after the direct physical loss. After you reopen, Extended Business Income runs up to 60 more days.
beats.say: Its period of restoration starts seventy-two hours after the direct physical loss. After you reopen, Extended Business Income runs up to sixty more days.

beats.text: Extra Expense pays extra costs to avoid or minimize the shutdown, like moving to a temporary location. It starts immediately.
beats.say: Extra Expense pays extra costs to avoid or minimize the shutdown, like moving to a temporary location. It starts immediately.

beats.text: So: lost profit while closed is Business Income. Extra money spent to keep going is Extra Expense.
beats.say: So: lost profit while closed is Business Income. Extra money spent to keep going is Extra Expense.

scenes.q: After a fire, a Traverse City dentist rents and equips a temporary office to keep seeing patients. Under the 2012 ISO form, which coverage pays, and when does it start?
scenes.why: Costs to keep operating from a temporary location are Extra Expense, which starts immediately. The 72-hour wait applies to Business Income.

beats.text: Try this. After a fire, a Traverse City dentist rents a temporary office to keep seeing patients. Which coverage pays, and when does it start? Pick an answer.
beats.say: Try this. After a fire, a Traverse City dentist rents a temporary office to keep seeing patients. Which coverage pays, and when does it start? Pick an answer.

reveal.text: Extra Expense, starting immediately. It's money spent to keep going. The 72-hour wait is only for Business Income.
reveal.say: Extra Expense, starting immediately. It's money spent to keep going. The seventy-two-hour wait is only for Business Income.

scenes.title: Other commercial property forms
items: Liability for others' property in your care

beats.text: A few more forms. The condominium association form is primary, and its insurer waives recovery against unit-owners. The commercial unit-owners form is excess over the association's insurance.
beats.say: A few more forms. The condominium association form is primary, and its insurer waives recovery against unit-owners. The commercial unit-owners form is excess over the association's insurance.

beats.text: Builders risk covers a building under construction, including materials meant to become part of it.
beats.say: Builders risk covers a building under construction, including materials meant to become part of it.

beats.text: The legal liability form covers your liability for others' property in your care, like a tenant's liability for the landlord's building.
beats.say: The legal liability form covers your liability for others' property in your care, like a tenant's liability for the landlord's building.

scenes.title: Selected endorsements
scenes.src: ISO CP 04 05 09 17, C.1-3; CP 04 40 06 07, A., C.3; CP 12 30 06 95; IRMI glossary 'reporting form coverage'

items.label: Ordinance or Law
items.detail: A: undamaged portion. B: demolition cost. C: increased cost of construction

items.label: Spoilage
items.detail: Perishable stock: refrigeration breakdown, refrigerant contamination, power outage

items.label: Peak Season Limit
items.detail: Higher personal property limit only during scheduled dates

items.label: Value Reporting
items.detail: For fluctuating values; premium based on the values reported

beats.text: Four endorsements. Ordinance or Law: A pays the loss to the undamaged portion, B pays demolition cost, and C pays the increased cost of construction.
beats.say: Four endorsements. Ordinance or Law: A pays the loss to the undamaged portion, B pays demolition cost, and C pays the increased cost of construction.

beats.text: Spoilage covers perishable stock for refrigeration breakdown or contamination, and for power outage.
beats.say: Spoilage covers perishable stock for refrigeration breakdown or contamination, and for power outage.

beats.text: Peak Season raises the personal property limit only during scheduled dates, like a toy store's holiday rush.
beats.say: Peak Season raises the personal property limit only during scheduled dates, like a toy store's holiday rush.

beats.text: Value Reporting suits fluctuating values like inventory. The limit is set for peak values, but premium is based on the values you report.
beats.say: Value Reporting suits fluctuating values like inventory. The limit is set for peak values, but premium is based on the values you report.

scenes.q: After a covered fire, city code requires an owner to tear down the undamaged part of the building. Which Ordinance or Law coverage pays to demolish it and clear the site?
scenes.why: Coverage B is demolition cost. Coverage A pays the loss to the undamaged portion, and Coverage C pays the increased cost of construction.

beats.text: Last one. After a covered fire, city code makes an owner tear down the undamaged part of the building. Which Ordinance or Law coverage pays for the demolition? Pick an answer.
beats.say: Last one. After a covered fire, city code makes an owner tear down the undamaged part of the building. Which Ordinance or Law coverage pays for the demolition? Pick an answer.

reveal.text: Coverage B, demolition cost. A is the loss to the undamaged portion, and C is the increased cost of construction.
reveal.say: Coverage B, demolition cost. A is the loss to the undamaged portion, and C is the increased cost of construction.

scenes.title: Key takeaways
items: Broad adds falling objects, snow and ice weight, water damage
Vacant over 60 days: some perils excluded, the rest cut 15%
Coinsurance: Did over Should, times loss, minus deductible
Business Income waits 72 hours; Extra Expense starts at once
Ordinance or Law: A undamaged part, B demolition, C code upgrade

beats.text: Let's recap. Broad adds falling objects, snow and ice weight, and water damage. Vacancy over 60 days excludes some perils and cuts the rest by 15%.
beats.say: Let's recap. Broad adds falling objects, snow and ice weight, and water damage. Vacancy over sixty days excludes some perils and cuts the rest by fifteen percent.

beats.text: Coinsurance is Did over Should. Business Income waits 72 hours. And Ordinance or Law runs A, B, C.
beats.say: Coinsurance is Did over Should. Business Income waits seventy-two hours. And Ordinance or Law runs A, B, C.
